macro.summary: BREAKING: US stock market futures extend losses as the US announces its 6th consecutive night of strikes on Iran.
China's GDP grew just +4.3% YoY in Q2 2026, the slowest pace in the current slowdown cycle.
The current bull run is historic: S&P 500 up +95% since end of 2022, placing it in the strongest 10% of bull markets at this stage since 1928 data begins.
Foreign holdings of US Treasuries rose +$18B in May to $9.37T, the 2nd-highest on record — demand for US debt still resilient despite fiscal/hawkish-Fed narrative.
AI is driving a historic boom in cybersecurity: global market expected to exceed $350B by 2030 (9.1% CAGR) as generative AI lowers the barrier to sophisticated attacks.
Kospi closed for a holiday but KORU still trading; zerohedge amplifying its own "Trend Is Now An Enemy: Kospi Slide Will Deepen" piece — South Korea market-risk watch continues.

US military completes its latest round of strikes against Iran (CENTCOM confirmed 9:40pm ET) — Iran conflict still escalating, not de-escalating as Trump's earlier "Iran wants a deal" comment implied.
Japan's Nikkei 225 slides -4% as tech slumps on "AI jitters" — first major Asian AI-leadership crack overnight.
"The Killer Chokepoint": China's rare-earth export squeeze reshaping the global economy — supply-chain risk piece.
Visualizing China's role in stabilizing oil markets — China cushioning global crude supply amid Iran/Hormuz disruption.
Fed Vice Chair Phil Jefferson entertains higher rates later this year in a speech on navigating economic shocks, while trying not to prejudge the meeting.
WSJ: Treasury's top tax-policy official was forced out after warning a potential White House tax-policy move [reported as fiscally risky] — quoting WSJ Politics reporting.
Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan sounds like someone prepared to vote for a rate increase in her remarks at a Dallas Fed event — third Fed official in 24h (with Jefferson) leaning hawkish.

No new tickers, but reinforces patience/selectivity over the AI/semi leadership group flagged yesterday.

stocks.ticker: SKHY (SK Hynix), Samsung Electronics, MU, INTC
stocks.note: Relays Meritz Securities analyst Kim Sunwoo: "This Is Not the Time to Sell Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix" — DRAM suppliers can fill only 75-80% of H2 2026 demand, falling to ~60% in 2027; 2027 P/E cited at 3.5x (Hynix) / 3.9x (Samsung). Adds Intel CEO's quote of "no relief in memory supply or pricing until at least 2028" and Micron's 16 favorable take-or-pay LTAs as corroboration. Continues yesterday's fundamentals-vs-price-disconnect thesis on memory names — bullish contrarian setup if the market catches up.

"My guess is we're close to market bottom on semis from $INTC $LITE. A good indicator is if everyone on $RDDT blew up their portfolios to $0" — semi-jocular capitulation/bottom-signal call on beaten-down semis/photonics names.

Reply noting the entire AI sector is dropping indiscriminately: $MRVL down -31%; higher-beta names like $AAOI and $SIVE seeing ~50% drops, but recoveries in these names historically come quickly too (tail truncated) — framing today's AI-sector selloff as overdone/high-beta noise rather than a fundamental break.

Reply: "my $EWY longs crashed quite a bit. I still think the operating income that SK Hynix and Samsung produce w[arrants holding]" — acknowledging near-term pain on Korea-exposed longs but maintaining the fundamentals thesis above.
